People ask me all the time whether the old town is overrated, and I never give the same answer twice. In August, honestly, it might be. You should see it at eight in the morning instead, when the shops are still closed and the stone is completely yours. My real advice is different, though. Give the coast two days, and then take the bus inland for one. Almost nobody does it. The villages up there are not unique in any dramatic way, but lunch is typical, it lasts three hours, and it costs half of what you pay by the water. That is the day people remember. Everything else they could have seen in a photograph.

I will argue the other side, because somebody has to. A place is not overrated simply because many people go there. The walls of Dubrovnik are unique, and there is no second version of them anywhere in Europe. What people really mean, I think, is that the experience is crowded, and that is a different complaint. So my honest opinion is this: you should pay for the guided walk at opening time. It costs more, it starts too early, and you might be tired. But you will stand on that stone with maybe thirty other people instead of three thousand, and then you can decide for yourself. Reconsider the hour, not the place.

First he read an article saying that the old town was overrated and not worth it any more. Then he went at noon in August and almost agreed, because he could hardly walk. The next morning he came back at seven and found the same street completely empty. That afternoon he took the bus inland, off the beaten track, and had a typical lunch that lasted three hours. In the end he reconsidered his whole opinion, and told his friends that the place was fine and the hour was the problem.
